report.summary: Chunk 1 of daedalus/structcore/index.py: module docstring describing output keys, opt-in flags for documents/types/wiki, and helper functions (_collect, _collect_docs, _py_dotted, _disambiguate, documents_enabled, types_enabled, wiki_enabled).
risks: _disambiguate | medium | The function may return None for ambiguous modules, causing dropped edges; callers must handle this gracefully. | Check that all callers of _disambiguate handle None return without crashing or silently skipping.

documents_enabled, types_enabled, wiki_enabled | low | Env var parsing uses _TRUTHY set; values like 'TRUE' or '1' are accepted, but unexpected values default to False. | Ensure that all expected truthy values are in _TRUTHY or that documentation clarifies accepted values.

handoff.purpose: Module-level docstring describing the build_index output, opt-in flags (documents, types, wiki), and helper functions for file collection and name disambiguation.

symbols.name: _collect
symbols.note: Walks root directory, yields (Path, rel, LanguageSpec) for code files, respecting _IGNORE_DIRS and max_files.

symbols.name: documents_enabled
symbols.note: Returns bool: explicit flag > env var > False.

symbols.name: types_enabled
symbols.note: Returns bool: explicit flag > env var > False.

symbols.name: wiki_enabled
symbols.note: Returns bool: explicit flag > env var > False.

symbols.name: _collect_docs
symbols.note: Separate walk for document files, returns (Path, rel, DocumentSpec).

symbols.name: _py_dotted
symbols.note: Converts a relative path like 'a/b/c.py' to 'a.b.c'.

symbols.name: _disambiguate
symbols.note: Given list of relative paths sharing a dotted name, returns the one that binds (preferring non-stub), or None if ambiguous.

symbols.name: _View
symbols.note: NamedTuple representing one importer's-eye view of the Python dotted namespace (incomplete in this chunk).

symbols.name: _IGNORE_DIRS
symbols.note: Set of directory names to skip during walk.

symbols.name: _DOC_ENV
symbols.note: Environment variable name for documents opt-in.

symbols.name: _TYPES_ENV
symbols.note: Environment variable name for types opt-in.

symbols.name: _WIKI_ENV
symbols.note: Environment variable name for wiki opt-in.

symbols.name: _TRUTHY
symbols.note: Set of strings considered truthy for env var parsing.

symbols.name: _STUB_SUFFIXES
symbols.note: Tuple of suffixes for stub files ('.pyi').

claims.text: Output: languages — files + LOC per language actually found
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the code that produces the 'languages' output; it only describes it.

claims.text: Output: modules — per-file health metrics

Output: dependencies / fan_in — internal import graph (Python precise; other languages best-effort via imports.py — module->file resolution is approximated without a real build graph, so unresolved edges are dropped, never guessed)
Output: duplication — exact (unit) + renamed (Type-2) + near-miss (Type-3) clone clusters, plus window-level (universal, parser-free)
Output: hotspots — complexity ranking, multiplied by normalized git churn (the CodeScene signal: rot lives where code is complex AND changing)
Output: backend — which optional precision engines were active
OPT-IN, absent unless documents=True (or DAEDALUS_INDEX_DOCUMENTS=1): documents — what was parsed, and everything it was withheld from
claims.why: The chunk defines documents_enabled() and _DOC_ENV, implementing the opt-in mechanism. The output itself is not produced in this chunk, but the claim about opt-in is kept.

claims.text: OPT-IN, absent unless documents=True: document_links / document_links_reverse — intra-repo markdown links, kept in their OWN relation layer because a link is not an import
With documents on, modules also carries document entries, each marked kind: "document" (markdown.is_document / code_modules).
OPT-IN, absent unless types=True (or DAEDALUS_INDEX_TYPES=1): types — the type/data-structure layer's counts and its own coverage record
claims.why: The chunk defines types_enabled() and _TYPES_ENV, implementing the opt-in mechanism.

claims.text: OPT-IN, absent unless types=True: type_nodes — one node per class/dataclass/TypedDict/NamedTuple/Enum/Protocol/alias declaration and per field, in their OWN id namespace
OPT-IN, absent unless types=True: type_edges — has_field / field_type / inherits / consumes / produces / alias_of, in their OWN relation layer
Type nodes NEVER enter modules, import_edges, dependencies, fan_in, all_units or the symbol resolver.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the code that builds those structures; it only declares the policy.

claims.text: Documents are excluded, always, from: all four clone passes, score_modules/hotspots/module_heat, import_edges/fan_in, and graph._graph_nodes.
Their links live in their own relation layer.

The type/data-structure layer is ADDITIVE by construction: it publishes three new keys and touches nothing that already existed. modules, import_edges, import_edges_reverse, fan_in, duplication, n_files, languages, total_tokens and hotspots are byte-identical with it on and with it off, and tests/test_typegraph_index.py pins exactly that.
claims.why: This chunk does not contain the code that produces those outputs, nor the test file.

claims.text: Gating extraction would put the flag on the wrong side of a content-keyed disk cache and a layer-off row would be served as a hit to a layer-on build — an empty type block with no error.
What the gate covers is whole-repo RESOLUTION (serial, in the parent, not cached) and PUBLICATION. Because the gate changes the returned dict, it is part of _scope_key exactly as documents is.

Type nodes are excluded, always, from: modules (so also hotspots / module_heat / score_modules), import_edges / import_edges_reverse / dependencies / fan_in, graph._graph_nodes (the fence's denominator), all_units and therefore all four clone passes, and graph.build_resolver's defs_by_file.

A separate walk rather than a second return value from _collect: _collect's (root, max_files) -> list signature is monkeypatched by tests/test_structcore_parallel.py to prove walk-order independence, and widening it would break that proof for a saving of one os.walk (~0.2s on a 7k-file tree, and only when documents are enabled at all).
claims.why: The chunk does not contain tests/test_structcore_parallel.py; the claim about monkeypatching is uncheckable.

claims.text: Order-independent by construction: the answer is a function of the SET of candidates, never of the order they were walked in.
claims.why: The function code does not depend on iteration order; it processes the list as a set via list comprehensions.

claims.text: The previous {_py_dotted(rel): rel for ...} dict comprehension was a last-writer-wins race decided by os.walk — measured at 141 live collisions on project_tct, every one a .py/.pyi pair, and it bound the name to the STUB.
claims.why: This claim refers to previous code not present in the chunk.

claims.text: Two rules, in order: 1. A stub is not a rival. If exactly one candidate is real source, the name is that module and the stub is its declaration. 2. Otherwise refuse.
claims.why: The function code implements exactly these two rules: first checks if len(rels)==1, then filters out stubs and checks if len(real)==1.

claims.text: A wrong edge lies about what depends on what — strictly worse than a missing one.
claims.why: This is a design rationale, not a checkable claim about the code in this chunk.

claims.text: Callers report the refusal with counts rather than binding to whichever file sorted first.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the caller code that would report counts.

observations.what: _collect and _collect_docs share similar structure but are separate functions to maintain monkeypatch compatibility.
_disambiguate returns None when multiple non-stub files claim the same dotted name, which could lead to dropped imports.
The env var parsing in documents_enabled, types_enabled, wiki_enabled uses the same _TRUTHY set; case-insensitive check via .lower().
_View NamedTuple is defined but its fields are not shown in this chunk (truncated at end).
